fields.title: Change a skill or a hook

sections.When to use this: You are editing a file under `template/.plugin/`, or one of the skills under `.claude/skills/`. Three trees, and what a change costs depends on which one. Every corpus here names `plugin.from` in its descriptor, so a skill under `template/.plugin/` is authored once and shipped in four plugins, and a change to it moves more version stamps than any other file here. A skill under `.claude/skills/` that `manifest.yaml` sends to a corpus travels into a working tree. Adding, removing or renaming one of those moves `version:` there and the stamp in every descriptor, and changing what one says moves neither. One nothing sends moves nothing.
sections.Prerequisites:
* [std-PLUGIN](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/8d79e9202a4b987e1dbc1c600543f5a0d15dab89/examples/dog-fooding/standards/plugin.md), which states the rules a bundled skill follows. It states no order, so this page supplies one.
* [std-VERS](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/8d79e9202a4b987e1dbc1c600543f5a0d15dab89/examples/dog-fooding/standards/versioning.md), which states what a move of each version stamp means.
* `kac` run as `dotnet run --project ../../tooling/kac --` from inside a corpus under `examples/`.
* A corpus declaring `consumes:` needs `kac restore` first. `restore` needs its producer packed.
* The [`writing-for-agents`](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/tree/v1.3.1/skills/productivity/writing-for-agents) skill, which step 3 loads. It is the reference std-PLUGIN cites for
  how a skill and its description are written.
* Writing a skill an agent follows, which step 4 needs.
* Judging which version stamps move, which steps 7 to 9 need.
